correctness.rationale: The source threshold beta2* is exactly B0[1−(1−sigma)x/(1+x)^2], x=alpha*sigma/mu, B0>0, 0<sigma<1. Differentiation yields ((1−sigma)(x−1))/(1+x)^3 with unique minimum B0(3+sigma)/4 at x=1, limits B0 as x→0+,∞. Solving (1−r)(1+x)^2=(1−sigma)x produces two positive reciprocal quadratic roots iff (3+sigma)/4<r<1; the inequality beta2>beta2* holds precisely between the roots. At r≤ minimum no strict backward inequality; r≥1 holds for every finite x>0. Independently checked derivative/quadratic rational identities. The original theorem concerns local bifurcation *at R0=1* while varying alpha with appropriate critical transmission parameter; no fixed-transmission global prevalence conclusion.

Critical rates, symmetry of endpoints and explicit limits permit parameter analysis of a natural bifurcation quantity; value rests on interpreting and classifying a meaningful model threshold rather than claiming algebra alone as new epidemiology.
